chapterNote: The great penitential psalm, wrung out of David after Nathan's 'You are the man' laid open the Bathsheba adultery and the murder of Uriah (2 Samuel 11-12). It is the anatomy of true repentance. David brings no excuses and no bargaining — only the full vocabulary of sin (pesha the rebellion, avon the twisted guilt, chattath the missed mark) laid against the fuller vocabulary of grace (chesed the covenant love, rachamim the womb-deep compassion). He asks for what only God can do: blot the record, wash the stain, and then go deeper than cleansing — create, bara, the Genesis word, a clean heart from nothing, for the old one is the problem. He knows ritual cannot carry this weight: You do not delight in sacrifice, or I would bring it; the sacrifice God will not despise is a broken and crushed heart. The psalm ends looking outward, as real repentance does — transgressors taught Your ways, sinners returning, Zion built up — because the forgiven man's mouth, once opened by the Lord Himself, cannot stay shut.

1.text: For the choir director. A psalm of David, when Nathan the prophet came to him after he had gone in to Bathsheba. Be gracious to me, O God, according to Your covenant love; according to the abundance of Your deep compassions, blot out my transgressions.
1.amp: To the chief Musician [natsach], A Psalm [mizmor] of David, when Nathan [Natan] the prophet [nabi] came [bo] unto him, after he had gone in [bo] to Bathsheba [Bat-Sheva]. Have mercy [chanan — be gracious] upon me, O God [Elohim], according to Your lovingkindness [chesed — covenant love]: according unto the multitude [rob] of Your tender mercies [rachamim — womb-deep compassions] blot out [machah — wipe away, erase] my transgressions [pesha — rebellions].
1.notes: The superscription names the wound; the same verb bo describes Nathan's coming and David's going in. The appeal is proportioned to God, not the sin: chesed (H2617) and rachamim (H7356), covenant loyalty and mother-deep compassion, in rob (H7230), multitude. machah (H4229) is to wipe a record clean, and pesha (H6588) is sin as open rebellion — named without softening.

2.text: Wash me through and through from my twisted guilt, and cleanse me from my sin.
2.amp: Wash [kabas — scrub as a launderer treads clothing] me throughly [rabah — multiply the washing] from my iniquity [avon — twisted guilt], and cleanse [taher — pronounce and make pure] me from my sin [chattath].
2.notes: kabas (H3526) is the fuller's word: laundry trodden and beaten clean, not rinsed. avon (H5771) is iniquity as twistedness with its guilt attached, chattath (H2403) sin as the missed mark, and taher (H2891) is the priest's verdict-word — David wants both the scrubbing and the pronouncement.

3.text: For I know my transgressions, and my sin is in front of me continually.
3.amp: For I acknowledge [yada — know] my transgressions [pesha]: and my sin [chattath] is ever [tamid] before me.
3.notes: yada (H3045): the knowing that finally stops managing the story. tamid (H8548) is the word for the perpetual offering — his sin had become his continual sacrifice, the thing always on the altar of his sight, likely through the long unrepentant year (cf. Psalm 32:3-4).

4.text: Against You, You only, have I sinned, and done what is evil in Your sight — so that You are proved right when You speak, and clear when You render judgment.
4.amp: Against You, You only, have I sinned [chata], and done [asah] this evil [ra] in Your sight [ayin]: that You might be justified [tsadaq — proved righteous] when You speak [dabar], and be clear [zakah — pure, blameless] when You judge [shaphat].
4.notes: David wronged Bathsheba, Uriah, and a kingdom — yet every sin's first offense is Godward, for only His law makes it SIN. tsadaq and zakah (H6663, H2135): the confession is written so that God's sentence, whatever it is, stands vindicated. Paul quotes this clause to prove God true though every man be a liar (cf. Romans 3:4).

5.text: Look at me: I was brought forth in iniquity, and in sin my mother conceived me.
5.amp: Behold, I was shapen [chul — brought forth in birth-writhing] in iniquity [avon]; and in sin [chet] did my mother [em] conceive ['warm me', yacham, the KJV margin] me.
5.notes: Not a slur on his mother but the oldest confession of original sin: the crookedness predates the deeds, running back through chul (H2342), the birth-writhing, to conception itself. The adultery was not an anomaly in an otherwise clean nature; it was the nature surfacing (cf. Psalm 58:3; Ephesians 2:3).

6.text: See, You desire truth in the inward parts, and in the hidden place You will make me know wisdom.
6.amp: Behold, You desire [chaphets] truth [emeth] in the inward parts [tuchah — the covered-over inmost being]: and in the hidden [satham] part You shall make me to know [yada] wisdom [chokmah].
6.notes: The counterweight to verse 5: sin runs to the core, so emeth (H571), truth, must be installed at the same depth — tuchah (H2910), the plastered-over inward places where the cover-up lived. God teaches chokmah in the very room where the lie was kept.

7.text: Purge my sin with hyssop, and I will be clean; wash me, and I will be whiter than snow.
7.amp: Purge [chata — un-sin] me with hyssop [ezov], and I shall be clean [taher]: wash [kabas] me, and I shall be whiter [laban] than snow [sheleg].
7.notes: The verb is literally 'un-sin me' (H2398 in its cleansing form). ezov (H231), hyssop, was the brush that applied Passover blood to the doorposts and sprinkled the leper clean (cf. Exodus 12:22; Leviticus 14:6-7) — David asks to be treated as what he is, a leper and a death-marked man, and the promised result outruns the request: whiter than sheleg (cf. Isaiah 1:18).

8.text: Let me hear joy and gladness again, so that the bones You have crushed may dance.
8.amp: Make me to hear [shama] joy [sason] and gladness [simchah]; that the bones [etsem] which You have broken [dakah — crushed] may rejoice [gil — exult, spin with joy].
8.notes: The broken etsem (H6106) are God's own doing — conviction as fracture, mercy wearing a cast. gil (H1523) is joy with motion in it: David asks that the very bones that ached under guilt (cf. Psalm 32:3) be the ones that dance.

9.text: Hide Your face from my sins, and wipe out all my twisted guilt.
9.amp: Hide [satar] Your face [panim] from my sins [chet], and blot out [machah] all mine iniquities [avon].
9.notes: The inversion that only grace dares: elsewhere the hidden panim (H6440) is the disaster (cf. Psalm 27:9); here David begs God to hide His face — from the sins, not the sinner. machah (H4229) returns from verse 1: the ledger wiped, every line.

10.text: Create in me a clean heart, O God, and make new a steadfast spirit within me.
10.amp: Create [bara] in me a clean [tahor] heart [leb], O God [Elohim]; and renew [chadash] a right ['constant', kun, the KJV margin — established, steadfast] spirit [ruach] within [qereb] me.
10.notes: bara (H1254) is the Genesis 1:1 verb, used only of God, always of making from nothing: David does not ask for repairs, he asks for ex nihilo — a leb tahor where none exists. kun (H3559) is firmness: a spirit that stands where the old one slid. This is the new-covenant promise prayed in advance (cf. Ezekiel 36:26).

11.text: Do not cast me out of Your presence, and do not take from me Your Holy Spirit.
11.amp: Cast me not away [shalak — throw, fling] from Your presence [panim]; and take [laqach] not Your holy [qodesh] Spirit [ruach] from me.
11.notes: David had watched the ruach qodesh (H7307, H6944) depart from Saul and the kingdom rot from the head down (cf. 1 Samuel 16:14) — this is a king praying not to become his predecessor. Under the new covenant the Spirit seals rather than visits (cf. Ephesians 1:13), but the dread of distance remains the mark of a living heart.

12.text: Give me back the joy of Your salvation, and let a willing spirit hold me upright.
12.amp: Restore [shub] unto me the joy [sason] of Your salvation [yesha]; and uphold [samak — support, sustain] me with Your free [nadiv — willing, noble, generous] spirit [ruach].
12.notes: What sin costs the believer first is not salvation but its sason (H8342), its joy — and shub (H7725), the repentance-verb itself, here asks God to do the returning. nadiv (H5081) is the willing nobility of a volunteer: obedience restored from duty to desire, with samak (H5564) as the daily holding-up.

13.text: Then I will teach transgressors Your ways, and sinners will come turning back to You.
13.amp: Then will I teach [lamad] transgressors [pasha — rebels] Your ways [derek]; and sinners [chatta] shall be converted [shub — turned back] unto You.
13.notes: 'Then' — restored men make the credible teachers, for the pasha (H6586) will listen to a fellow rebel who found mercy. lamad (H3925) and shub (H7725): Psalm 51 itself is the fulfillment of this vow, having turned more sinners home than perhaps any other song.

14.text: Deliver me from the guilt of shed blood, O God, God of my salvation, and my tongue will sing aloud of Your righteousness.
14.amp: Deliver [natsal] me from bloodguiltiness ['bloods', dam, the KJV margin], O God [Elohim], You God of my salvation [teshuah]: and my tongue [lashon] shall sing aloud [ranan — ring out with joy] of Your righteousness [tsedaqah].
14.notes: damim, 'bloods' plural: Uriah's murder named at last, the sin beneath the sin (cf. 2 Samuel 12:9). The law had no sacrifice for deliberate murder — only Elohim teshuati (H8668), the God of my salvation, can clear it. And the cleared tongue's first note is His tsedaqah (H6666), not its own relief.

15.text: O Lord, open these lips of mine, and my mouth will show forth Your praise.
15.amp: O Lord [Adonai], open [pathach] You my lips [saphah]; and my mouth [peh] shall show forth [nagad — declare] Your praise [tehillah].
15.notes: Guilt had shut the singer's mouth; only Adonai (H136) can pathach (H6605) it again. The line the church has prayed at the start of daily worship for fifteen centuries — every act of praise begins as His unlocking.

16.text: For You take no delight in sacrifice, or I would bring it; You have no pleasure in burnt offering.
16.amp: For You desire [chaphets] not sacrifice [zebach]; else would I give [natan] it: You delight [ratsah] not in burnt offering [olah].
16.notes: Not a repeal of the sacrificial system but its exposure: for adultery and murder the altar had no tariff, and even where it did, the zebach (H2077) was never the thing itself (cf. 1 Samuel 15:22; Hosea 6:6). David would gladly pay any olah (H5930); the price is not payable in livestock.

17.text: The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit; a heart broken and crushed to dust, O God, You will not despise.
17.amp: The sacrifices [zebach] of God [Elohim] are a broken [shabar — shattered] spirit [ruach]: a broken and a contrite [dakah — crushed] heart [leb], O God, You will not despise [bazah].
17.notes: The altar God accepts: a ruach shabar (H7665) and a leb crushed to dakah (H1794), powder-fine. bazah (H959), despise — men despise broken things; God draws near to them (cf. Psalm 34:18; Isaiah 66:2). The one sacrifice a sinner can always afford is the one God never refuses.

18.text: In Your good pleasure do good to Zion; build up the walls of Jerusalem.
18.amp: Do good [yatab] in Your good pleasure [ratson — favor, delight] unto Zion [Tsiyyon]: build [banah] You the walls [chomah] of Jerusalem [Yerushalaim].
18.notes: The king's sin had breached more than his own soul — a shepherd's fall opens the whole fold. So repentance widens into intercession: yatab (H3190) for Tsiyyon (H6726), walls rebuilt by God's ratson (H7522), not David's management. Personal revival and the city's welfare rise together.

19.text: Then You will delight in sacrifices offered in righteousness, in burnt offering whole and entire; then bulls will ascend on Your altar.
19.amp: Then shall You be pleased [chaphets] with the sacrifices [zebach] of righteousness [tsedek], with burnt offering [olah] and whole [kalil] burnt offering: then shall they offer [alah] bullocks [par] upon Your altar [mizbeach].
19.notes: The altar returns — but only 'then', after the broken heart of verse 17: ritual reborn as the overflow of repentance rather than its substitute. zebach tsedek (H2077, H6664), sacrifices of righteousness, offered by clean hands in a rebuilt city: worship set back in its right order, inside out.
